ecological_importance: Acts as an important ruderal weed supporting localized insect herbivores and serving as a well-known stimulant for domestic cats.
threats: None; often managed as a weed in cultivated gardens.
conservation_actions: Maintained in biodiversity corners as an ethnobotanically significant ruderal native plant.
field_identification_notes: Slender herbaceous weed found abundantly in waste places and roadsides.
Alternate ovate leaves with serrated margins and 3-5 basal veins.
Distinctive cup-shaped, folded green bracts enclosing tiny flowers in dangling axillary spikes.
ml_relevance: Ovate-rhomboid leaves with serrated margins and axillary dangling flower spikes with cup-shaped bracts.

ar_information.quick_identification: Slender annual herb; ovate leaves; unique cup-shaped bracts enclosing small flower spikes.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Ruderal colonizer; favored by domestic felines; supports micro-insects.
ar_information.conservation_message: Not Evaluated / Common Weed. Known in Tamil Nadu as Kuppaimeni, valued historically in traditional dermatology.

vit_campus_relevance.location: Waste lands, grassy borders, and unpaved pathways
